feedback.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(1,4,-2)$ and $Q(5,3,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(1,4,-2)$ and $Q(5,3,0).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+4t \\ 4-t \\ -2+2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+4t \\ y=4-t \\ z=-2+2t\end{aligned}
$$
